citation: 'Wilmette, IL', The Electronic Encyclopedia of Chicago (Chicago Historical Society, Newberry Library and Northwestern University, 2005), entry 1360.
author: The Electronic Encyclopedia of Chicago
rights_note: Modern encyclopedia text, cited in words only.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-30 (T-3251) through a fetch that returned the opening in short quoted fragments.
note: Fragments read: 'The village of Wilmette is named for Antoine Ouilmette, a French-Canadian fur trader' who settled at Chicago in 1790, and 'his part- Potawatomi wife, Archange Chevallier'; after Ouilmette helped secure the 1829 Treaty of Prairie du Chien 'the government deeded 1,280 acres, encompassing much of present-day Wilmette and part of Evanston' to Archange and her children.
what_it_supplies: Wilmette named for Antoine Ouilmette and his part-Potawatomi wife Archange Chevallier
the 1,280 acres deeded to Archange and her children after the 1829 treaty
what_it_does_not_supply: Archange's kinship to Catherine Chevalier Robinson, which the Indigenous Chicago profile of Alexander Robinson gives
